speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with yellowish discoloration of the skin; how many hours or days old is the baby when this jaundice first became noticeable?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since the baby is exclusively breastfed and there have been no changes in stool or urine, I need to assess his hydration and feeding intake: how many wet diapers has he passed today, and are you having any trouble getting him to latch or finish feeds? Also, has he had any episodes of vomiting or fever since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (also known as Suboptimal Intake Jaundice).

REQUEST TEST: Serum Total Bilirubin and Direct/Indirect Bilirubin fractionation.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound to rule out biliary atresia if direct bilirubin is elevated.
